text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Sources: Palestinian Authority might initiate violent confrontations again.
- Furious reactions to central bank governor's decision not to lower interest rates.
- U.S. initiative to lower Israeli-Egyptian tensions -- closer relations between army chiefs; Egypt weighing recall of its ambassador in Tel Aviv over Hebron deal delay.
- New interministerial team appointed to examine El Al privatisation.
- Fears that Arafat planning anti-Israeli disturbances.
- Sharp drop in new home sales in November.
- Netanyahu: Netzarim junction in Gaza is touchstone for Hebron.
- Labour party leaders meet in bid to defuse tensions.
- High Court upholds law barring import of non-kosher meat.
- Netanyahu blames Palestinian Authority for Hebron stalemate as talks resume.
- Applied Materials to acquire Orbot, Opal for $285 million in cash.
- Bank of Israel Governor Frenkel decides interest rates to remain unchanged.
- Two (unidentified) foreign companies interested in buying El Al.
